evidence.description: The response and error parameters are ignored, and any returned data is turned into an Item, published, and cached without validation.

candidates.explanation: The download completion handler discards both the response and the error, treating any non-nil data as a successful image download. HTTP error response bodies can therefore be published and cached, while failures without data produce no notification to the subscriber.
candidates.title: Download failures and HTTP status are ignored

evidence.description: Every cache miss starts a download without checking whether that URL is already being downloaded.
Cancellation selects only the first task matching the URL.
An item is inserted into the cache only after its data has arrived.

candidates.explanation: Only completed downloads are represented in the cache. Repeated loads for the same URL before completion each start another task, duplicating network work. The URL-specific cancellation method cancels only the first matching task, leaving other downloads for that URL running.
candidates.title: Duplicate in-flight downloads are not tracked

evidence.description: The instance owns a persistent set of cached items.
Completed downloads are inserted into the set without removing existing cached entries.
Each retained item contains the full downloaded Data.

candidates.explanation: The cache retains the complete Data payload for every distinct downloaded URL and has no eviction or clearing path in this class. Memory consumption can therefore continue growing as additional URLs are loaded for the lifetime of an Images instance.
candidates.title: Downloaded data accumulates without eviction

evidence.description: The cache is searched with a predicate over its elements.
Item hashing and equality both use URL, but the lookup does not use the set's hashed membership operations.

candidates.explanation: Although items are stored in a Set whose hash and equality are based on URL, cache lookup uses first(where:), which performs a linear search rather than a hash lookup. Each load can examine the entire cache, making lookup cost grow with the number of cached URLs.
candidates.title: Cache lookup bypasses the set's hash indexing
